summary:
Smart Crop Rotation 2.0 (Rotação Inteligente 2.0) is an open-access agricultural intelligence platform engineered to transform NASA Earth Observations into climate-resilient, soil-restoring crop rotation strategies for global producers.
Built upon a modern decoupled architecture (FastAPI + React 19), the platform assimilates 35 years of daily satellite and reanalysis records (NASA POWER, SRTM, NOAA ONI) through established biophysical models (FAO-56 Hargreaves–Samani, USDA-SCS, and FAO-33). Utilizing the NSGA-II multi-objective evolutionary algorithm, the engine navigates the Pareto frontier to benchmark the grower’s current practice against tailored strategies for maximum soil conservation, water resilience, and farmer-weighted balance across a 24-month horizon and a 13-crop functional catalog.
Featuring a delta-perturbation climate sensitivity simulator (ΔT and ΔP), structured infeasibility diagnostics, and end-to-end evidence traceability without inflated production promises, the project fulfills the core mission of NASA’s Field Shift Challenge: delivering transparent, farmer-centric decision support anchored in open space science.
details:
Rotação Inteligente 2.0 is an agricultural intelligence and decision-support platform that transforms historical Earth observation and climate modeling data into environmental diagnostics, climate sensitivity simulations, and 24-month crop rotation plans.

  1. Location & Farm Setup: Users select a location via coordinates or an interactive map (reverse-geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim, with optional SRTM 90m slope estimation via OpenTopoData and visual NASA GIBS layers such as MODIS NDVI, GPM IMERG, and SMAP L4) and provide optional soil, slope, irrigation, current rotation, and priority preferences.
  2. Climate & Vulnerability Analysis: The FastAPI backend fetches and caches daily historical series (1991–2025/2026) from NASA POWER and NOAA/CPC ONI v6 ENSO data. It computes reference evapotranspiration (ET0ET_0ET0​ via Hargreaves–Samani / FAO-56), effective rainfall (USDA-SCS/CROPWAT), extreme climate indices (dry spells, Tmax⁡≥35∘CT_{\max} \ge 35^\circ\text{C}Tmax​≥35∘C, Rx1day, Rx5day, R20mm), Theil–Sen/Mann–Kendall trends, and an 8-indicator experimental vulnerability index (0–1 scale).
  3. 24-Month Optimization: Modeling a 24-month circular calendar (up to four non-overlapping planting slots) across sliding two-year historical windows (34 pairs / 68 crop-year observations), the engine evaluates crop water balance (ETcET_cETc​, ETaET_aETa​, FAO-33 KyK_yKy​ potential relative yield loss) and thermal stress across a 13-crop catalog. Using NSGA-II (pymoo), it generates a Pareto front of trade-offs and presents Strategies A–D alongside climate/irrigation sensitivity simulations, auditable rule-based justifications, and exportable Markdown/print reports.

What benefits does it offer?

  • Multi-Year Perspective: Replaces isolated single-season guesswork with 24-month rotational planning that accounts for soil cover, crop diversity, and carry-over climate risk.
  • Transparent Trade-Offs: Lets farmers, technicians, and researchers compare competing goals—water efficiency, climate risk, soil health, erosion control, and diversification—on a Pareto frontier.
  • Scientific Traceability: Clearly separates measured/modeled data, literature parameters, and prototype assumptions, pairing outputs with evidence-completeness scores rather than black-box recommendations.
  • Scenario Testing & Reporting: Enables rapid "what-if" testing under altered temperature, rainfall, or irrigation conditions, with reproducible reports for rural extension and cooperatives.

What is the intended impact?

In the near term, the project aims to give farmers, cooperatives, agricultural technicians, students, and rural extension teams an accessible, transparent tool to design climate-resilient crop rotations. Long term, we aim to validate and expand the platform by integrating NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections, converting satellite layers (SMAP, IMERG, Landsat/HLS NDVI) into numerical inputs, adopting a dynamic soil water-balance model, calibrating crop parameters (KcK_cKc​, KyK_yKy​, and planting windows) through field trials with agronomic institutions, adding an economic module (costs, prices, and margins), and hardening the system for multi-user deployment.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: Python (3.10+) and JavaScript.
  • Backend & Optimization: FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pymoo (NSGA-II), and requests.
  • Frontend & Visualization: React 19, Vite 7, Tailwind CSS 4, Recharts, Leaflet, and React Leaflet.
  • Storage & Legacy Integration: SQLite (for saved properties and local caches) and a legacy Streamlit app (rotacao_inteligente/) sharing selected NASA POWER and ENSO modules.
  • External Data & APIs: NASA POWER (AG community), NOAA/CPC ONI v6, OpenTopoData (SRTM 90m), OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and NASA GIBS.
  • Testing & Tooling: pytest, httpx, Node.js built-in test runner (node --test), Git/GitHub, VS Code, and standard Windows/Linux development hardware.

What is the creative aspect of your project?

Instead of recommending a single crop from static climate averages, our project treats crop planning as a 24-month circular calendar evaluated across 34 sliding two-year historical windows, capturing interannual variability and carry-over effects. It creatively pairs NSGA-II multi-objective optimization with auditable, rule-based explainability (Strategies A–D, an experimental Soil Environmental Debt indicator, and evidence-completeness scoring). Additionally, when no rotation satisfies all constraints, the system provides a structured infeasibility diagnostic explaining exactly which agronomic or climatic bottleneck caused the failure rather than returning a generic error.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Agroclimatic & Hydrological Factors: Daily rainfall, effective rainfall, ET0ET_0ET0​ (chosen via Hargreaves–Samani because wind speed is absent from the input series), crop water deficit (KyK_yKy​), dry spells, extreme heat (≥35∘C\ge 35^\circ\text{C}≥35∘C), cold/frost thresholds, and ENSO associations.
  • Soil, Topography & Management: Optional soil attributes (texture, depth, organic matter, pH), SRTM 90m slope, erosion potential (Modified Fournier Index), soil cover fraction, 24-month irrigation budgets, and user priorities.
  • Strict Agronomic Constraints: No overlapping crops, at least one commercial crop per year, minimum 20 mm median rainfall in the first 30 days for rainfed crops, no consecutive same-species repetition, and cold-day limits.
  • Scientific Honesty & Operational Limits: Explicit caveats on regional satellite/reanalysis resolution, assumed Ky=1.0K_y = 1.0Ky​=1.0 for six uncalibrated species, non-independent sliding windows, absence of yield-in-kg/profit predictions, API rate limits (Nominatim 1.1 s lock and local SQLite caching), and prototype security boundaries.
